parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: With reference to Fig. 2.1, explain how the molecules of collagen are arranged **and** held together in a collagen fibril.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Suggest **two** properties of collagen that contribute to the function of cartilage in the trachea in the gas exchange system.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State the function of elastic fibres in the alveoli in the lungs.

parts.label: (c)
(c)(i)
parts.text: Complete Table 2.1 to show the amino acids coded by the DNA nucleotide sequence in Table 2.1.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The sequence of amino acids that you have worked out is representative of the whole of the collagen polypeptide.

Explain how the sequence of amino acids makes the polypeptide suitable as a component of a collagen molecule.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
Two mutations, **P** and **Q**, can have an effect on the primary structure of the polypeptide.
- Mutation **P** is a deletion of the first nucleotide pair in the DNA nucleotide sequence shown in Table 2.1.
- Mutation **Q** is a substitution of G with T as the first base in the DNA nucleotide sequence shown in Table 2.1.
State the effects of the mutations, **P** and **Q**, on the primary structure of the polypeptide.
